sections.label: President's Office Civil List increase
sections.summary: The President's Office proposes raising Class II and Class III Civil List sums, leaving Class I and Class IV unchanged, to cover manpower and IT costs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The President's Office has been able to manage within its budget by re-allocating savings across expenditure across Classes II, III and IV.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: To enable the President's Office to continue to meet its expenditure needs, I propose to vary the sums in Class II and Class III of the Civil List.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The provisions for Class I expenditures relating to the President's salary and entertainment allowance and Class IV expenditures concerning special services will remain unchanged.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The proposed increase more than 10 years later is to cater for increases in expenditure on manpower, including the Civil Service salary adjustments announced last year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Therefore, I propose an increase from $4,532,400, to $6,696,700 for Class II expenditures.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: For Class III expenditures, which provide for the expenses of household, I propose an increase from $2,762,300 to $3,342,200.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: This is to cater for higher IT costs, including IT security.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We expect this round of increase to be sufficient for up to FY2025.
